thread.title: Will Tech Stocks Fail Us? - PowerShares QQQ Trust ETF (NASDAQ:QQQ)

author: Dividend Investors
title: Will Tech Stocks Fail Us? - PowerShares QQQ Trust ETF (NASDAQ:QQQ)
text:
Image Source
Stock markets have had a very interesting year in 2018. Many of the previous trends that failed us in the past seemed to work in the bullish rally lead-up which creates this moment in time. But this does not necessarily mean that those trends will continue. Many have argued that investors became too complacent in the run-up to new record highs in the PowerShares NASDAQ Trust (NASDAQ: QQQ ). If this is actually what created most of the “flash crash” activity that defined tech trades in the early parts of this year, we can reasonably assume that some portions of the market will start looking the other way if this happens again in H2 2018. In terms of broader portfolio strategies, it will be key for investors to continue monitoring these areas when making assessments on which to base new strategies in individual stocks. When answering the question of whether tech stocks will fail the markets (or lead us higher) we can first look to the most recent valuation trends relative to the ETF’s longer-term valuation trends. We remain long QQQ as a portfolio diversifier and here we will look at a few of the factors that could influence price direction in the ETF as we head into 2019.
Stock Price Chart: CNN Money
Over the last five years, QQQ has posted gains of 132.94%. In the chart above, we can see that there has been very little in the way of material declines - and this has strengthened the validity of the alternative bearish stance for those have already started to bet against equities. Is it appropriate for tech stocks (or any other asset class, for that matter) to see gains that are this one-sided? We would like to see characteristics that are more corrective in any rally - but it does look as though this horse still has legs to run. In other words, our view is that there will likely be further gains in QQQ before we see anything that resembles an actual bear market.
Of course, the exact definition of what a bear market actually means is something that lies in the eye of the beholder. So, it is possible that there are viewpoints that actually support the outlook which suggests any sort of flash crash activity is, in and of itself, confirmation that a top is in place in stock markets.
FANG Stocks Chart: Bloomberg
The FANG stocks tend to be viewed as a leading indicator for what is more broadly expressed through the holdings of QQQ, and this is often accurate because these stocks make up more than one-third of the fund’s holdings. The FANG names generated their largest sell-offs ever as most of the volatility was occurring in the NASDAQ and in the Dow Jones Industrials. This begs the question of whether even deeper declines could be possible in the second half of the year.
AAPL Chart Analysis: Dividend-Investments.com
Whenever we are looking at potential momentum drivers in QQQ, it is hard to overlook Apple, Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL ). The tech innovator is the ETF’s top holding at a massive 12.01% of the allocation. Apple’s results for the second quarter showed per-share earnings at $2.73 and $61.1 billion in revenues. The company announced $100 billion in stock buybacks and a 16% dividend increase, which are both factors that should be viewed as favorable by long-term tech investors. Apple sold 52.2 million iPhones sold during the March quarter (a 3% rise on an annualized basis) but there were sections of the market that were hoping for better growth, and this is something that could weigh on this portion of the QQQ allocation if these weakening trends continue.
CSCO Chart Analysis: Dividend-Investments.com
Of course, the QQQ ETF is more than the FANG stock collective - and one of the most interesting holdings in our view continues to be Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO ). When we outlined our initial stance on Cisco, most investors were reluctant to believe that a bullish outbreak in the aging tech giant was even possible during this seemingly late-stage phases of its corporate growth outlook. Our individual projections for CSCO have turned out to be exceedingly accurate, and the next major market mover will likely be seen after the market close on May 16. We actually believe that a positive earnings surprise from Cisco could have a greater impact on QQQ than might be expected given its lower allocation weighting (at only 2.8%).
CSCO Earnings History: Zacks
Part of the reason for this lies in the fact CSCO has a strong history of rallying after its earnings releases (shown in the chart above). For the fiscal third-quarter, CSCO is expected to report per-share earnings of 65 cents and $12.4 billion in revenues. We expect strong moves higher here if CSCO is able to beat these numbers.
Tech Sector Earnings: Bloomberg
In this last chart, we can see that there is a major disconnect between the perception and the reality in the world of tech. Even as market prices have posted drastic declines (our flash crash scenarios), we have still seen steady improvements in the fundamental outlook. Profit estimates for the tech space have shown incredibly strong uptrends, and this supports our view that the companies contained within the QQQ ETF will likely be the main drivers of corporate growth as we head into 2019. With all of this in mind, we believe that tech will lead the market (and not fail the market) over this period. We remain long QQQ and plan to hold the ETF well into next year.
What is your position on QQQ? We look forward to reading your comments. Stay tuned to Dividend Investors and receive our next alerts by clicking the "Follow" button at the top of the page.
Disclosure: I am/we are long QQQ.
